title: runtime: model-aware KV-eviction + kernel-routing for Llama MQA latency cliffs
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Motivation: Several internal benchmarks and a customer report (SUP-783) surfaced a recurring performance cliff for Llama-family models when using MQA/GQA variants at long-context and bursty request patterns. The root causes we observed: 1) the generic KV-cache eviction policy aggressively slices recent KV segments for variable stride patterns in MQA, causing cache churn and repeated kernel warmups; 2) the kernel selector falls back to generic attention kernels when sequence-length / head-layout combos are observed during runtime, which amplifies latency spikes under continuous-batching. This PR introduces model-aware heuristics and a small runtime surface to stabilize latencies without changing public APIs.
changes_summary: Add per-model hinting and heuristic KV-eviction (age+stride scoring), extend kernel selector with model-layout preference, integrate continuous-batching guardrail that biases batching window based on per-model latency curve. Add targeted unit tests and bench harness; add observability metrics for eviction hits and kernel-switch count. Documentation for ops and rollout notes included.
commits: feat(runtime): add model_hint structure to model registry with kv_slice_preference and kernel_preferences
feat(kv): implement age+stride scoring and soft-eviction threshold; expose eviction metrics
perf(kernel_selector): prefer tiled-gqa kernel for qwen/mistral when layout matches; add fallback counters
feat(batch): continuous-batching guardrail that switches batching window per-model when tail latency >= SLO
test: add integration bench for MQA sustained sequences and unit tests for eviction scoring
docs: ops guide + rollout checklist for canary
review_comments: Evan Turner: Can you add a short e2e canary plan that specifies the canary traffic percentage and ramp schedule? The eviction thresholds feel like they could be sensitive to workload—we should be conservative for initial rollout.
Priya Kapoor: Added canary plan to docs and set default ramp to 5% -> 25% over 48h with rollback triggers based on p99 and kernel-switch-rate.
Lina Morales: The age+stride scoring function looks fine but please add a short comment explaining the tradeoff and why we picked soft-eviction vs hard slicing to avoid future regressions.
Priya Kapoor: Added inline comments and extra unit test covering stride=4 vs stride=1 pathological pattern.
Samir Patel: CI bench failed first run (bench-smoke) due to environment mismatch; tests rerun and passed. Approving after rerun.
Release Engineer (bot): Verified manifest change respects semver-like model manifest format; no breaking fields detected.
bench_results_summary: Sustained MQA workloads: 14% median token-cost reduction and 18% p99 latency improvement on our CI canary harness with 2k concurrent short-tail sequences. Worst-case sequences (stride mismatch) no longer show >2x latency spikes after heuristic enabled.
ops_rollout_notes: Canary rollout: enable on dedicated-canary pool; 5% traffic for 6h, monitor p50/p95/p99 and kernel_switch_rate, then 25% for 42h. Automatic rollback triggers: p99 increase >10% vs baseline OR kernel_switch_rate > 500 switches/min. Post-canary: gradual global flip with identical thresholds. Config knobs exposed: models.registry.<model>.kv_slice_preference, kernel_selector.prefer_layout, continuous_batcher.window_ms.{min,max}.
release_notes: Stabilize Llama MQA/GQA latency by adding model-specific KV eviction heuristics and kernel routing. Improves p99 for long-context MQA traffic and reduces kernel thrash under continuous batching. No API changes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: incorrect heuristics could worsen tail latency for uncommon workloads. Mitigation: default heuristics are conservative (soft eviction multiplier 0.6), a canary rollout with strict rollback rules, runtime flags to disable per-model routing, and additional observability (eviction_hit/miss, kernel_switch_count) to diagnose.
notes_for_release_manager: Flag as candidate for next minor; include in release notes under runtime/perf. Ops should coordinate canary on Dedicated clusters first (reserved GPU pools) because behavior depends on kernel availability. No infra schema migrations required.
